subject: MSA & Order Form: tax jurisdiction, licensing fee mapping, and portal signer escalation
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on MSA tax jurisdiction + portal field mapping

Hi Irene,

Thanks for sending over the MSA and the updated order form redlines (received yesterday). Our procurement team flagged two items that we need clarity on before we can proceed with portal activation in Ariba:

1) Tax / withholding jurisdiction: the MSA sets license fees as payable to Redwood in the US, but our AP needs to know which tax jurisdiction to apply in the portal (for VAT/EUTax/VAT reverse charge). Is there a canonical jurisdiction field that your portal maps to on the order form?

2) Signer provenance: our internal policy requires a named signatory on the order form to match the portal account admin. The redlines mention signature delegation but don’t map the signer role to any portal attribute.

We attached a short field inventory and the redline PDF for reference. Can your legal/ops folks confirm where these map (and whether you accept EU invoicing as a substitute jurisdiction declaration)?

Appreciate a quick note — we are gating onboarding to a Sept month-end payroll run.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Lead — NovaMed

Attachments: redlines_v3.docx, portal_field_map.csv

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@novamed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-09-25T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA tax jurisdiction + portal field mapping

Hi Elena — thanks for flagging this. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Jonas (Onboarding/Integrations) to confirm the fields and legal treatment.

Quick answers while they chime in:
- For Ariba/Coupa we have an Order Form field called "Billing Jurisdiction" that controls invoice routing. Historically we populate that with the billing country from the signed order form; legal needs to confirm whether that implies tax jurisdiction.
- For signer provenance we usually require the signatory name in the order form "SignedBy" attribute and match it to the portal account admin email at activation. If NovaMed requires the signatory to be a specific corporate officer, we can add that as a gating attribute in the activation checklist.

Marissa / Jonas — can you confirm whether Redwood accepts an EU invoicing declaration (i.e., invoice issued from Redwood EU entity) as sufficient for NovaMed's VAT handling, or do we need a contractual jurisdiction amendment on the MSA? Also, can Jonas confirm which portal field we should use to carry the jurisdiction value so NovaMed's AP team gets correct tax handling?

Will get back in one hour.

Thanks,
Irene
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-09-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA tax jurisdiction + portal field mapping

Irene / team — quick legal take:

- Current MSA (Redwood global master) routes payment to Redwood Inc. (US). For EU customers we have an EU invoicing option via Redwood Europe Ltd; that is handled operationally (invoicing entity selection) rather than by changing the MSA jurisdiction clause.
- If NovaMed needs explicit contract language that the governing law/tax residency is EU for the transaction we can add a one-line amendment to the Order Form referencing Redwood Europe Ltd as invoicing party. That avoids re-negotiating MSA governing law.
- For procurement portals, the critical piece is a durable field mapping: we must ensure the portal Order Form "InvoiceEntity" (or equivalent) is populated so AP can route invoice to the EU entity.

Kimberly — Legal would like to route the requested amendment as an order-form addendum (Order Form Exhibit A) rather than an MSA amendment. Any concern with signatory delegation if we do the addendum?

Marissa
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-09-25T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA tax jurisdiction + portal field mapping

Irene/Marissa — Operational mapping notes from onboarding:

- Ariba: we can map the order form field "custom:invoice_entity" to drive invoice routing. In practice we populate it with one of: "Redwood Inc (US)", "Redwood Europe Ltd (IE)", or "Redwood APAC Pte Ltd" depending on customer selection.
- Coupa: the equivalent is the "Bill To: Tax Jurisdiction" + custom field "rdw_invoice_entity". We'll add a portal validation rule so activation cannot complete until that custom field is set.
- Signer provenance: in our activation workflow we can require the "SignedBy" attribute to match the portal admin email (exact match). If NovaMed requires a named officer, we can add that as a conditional gating attribute and flag the order if mismatch.

Action items I propose:
1) Legal prepares a one-line order-form addendum that designates the invoicing entity (if NovaMed chooses EU entity).
2) Onboarding will add a portal validation rule to require rdw_invoice_entity or custom:invoice_entity filled at activation.
3) Sales to collect the signatory name and admin email at PO submission for verification.

Irene — I can implement the validation rule today if Marissa signs off on the addendum language.

Thanks,
Jonas
Onboarding Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-09-25T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA tax jurisdiction + portal field mapping

Marissa — that approach makes sense. A few drafting notes for the order-form addendum (to avoid confusion):

- Suggested language (single sentence): "For the purposes of invoicing and tax treatment under this Order Form, the Parties agree that invoices may be issued by Redwood Europe Ltd and that such designation shall determine the invoicing entity without amending the governing law of the MSA."
- Include a checkbox on the order form: "I confirm NovaMed requests invoicing from Redwood Europe Ltd" with a required typed signatory name and title. That gives procurement the named officer provenance they want.
- We should also include a fallback: if checkbox not selected, default remains Redwood Inc.

Once you approve I will drop this into redlines_v3.docx and track for signature.

Kimberly
Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com>, ProcureOps <procureops@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-09-25T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on MSA tax jurisdiction + portal field mapping

Hi Elena — thanks for waiting. Quick summary and next steps: 

1) Legal will add a one-line Order Form addendum that lets NovaMed select Redwood Europe Ltd as the invoicing entity (no MSA governing-law change). See draft language attached; we've put it into redlines_v3.docx.
2) Onboarding will add a portal validation rule so Ariba/Coupa activation requires the invoice entity field (custom:invoice_entity / rdw_invoice_entity) to be set.
3) Procurement checkbox: we will add the checkbox and require the typed signatory name + title as provenance for the signer. That will be validated against the portal admin email at activation; if mismatch, activation will flag and require manual override.

Action for you: please confirm whether you want invoices issued by "Redwood Europe Ltd (IE)" or "Redwood Inc (US)" and provide the intended signatory name and their email for matching in the portal. If you confirm today we will: (a) send the amended order form (DocuSign link) for signature, and (b) schedule a 30-minute activation window with Onboarding.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/example123
Shared docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-docs

Thanks again — we understand the payroll timing constraint and will prioritize same-day execution when you confirm.

Best,
Irene
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
